chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Abū ʿAlī Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥārith al-Qazwīnī narrated to me, saying:

I was with my father in Surrā man Raʾā, and my father used to practice veterinary work in the stable of Abū Muḥammad. He said: Al-Mustaʿīn had a mule the like of which had not been seen in beauty and size, and it would refuse its back, the bridle, and the saddle. Trainers had been gathered against it, but it gave them no means to ride it.

He said: One of his close companions said to him, "O Commander of the Faithful, why do you not send for al-Ḥasan ibn al-Riḍā so that he may come? Either he will ride it, or it will kill him, and you will be relieved of him."

He said: So he sent for Abū Muḥammad, and my father went with him. My father said: When Abū Muḥammad entered the residence, I was with him. Abū Muḥammad looked at the mule standing in the courtyard of the house, then turned toward it and placed his hand on its croup. He said: I looked at the mule, and it had sweated until perspiration flowed from it. Then he went to al-Mustaʿīn and greeted him. He welcomed him and brought him near, then said, "O Abū Muḥammad, bridle this mule." So Abū Muḥammad said to my father, "Bridle it, O boy." Al-Mustaʿīn said, "You bridle it." So he put down his cloak, then stood and bridled it, then returned to his seat and sat down.

Then he said to him, "O Abū Muḥammad, saddle it." So he said to my father, "O boy, saddle it." He said, "You saddle it." So he stood a second time and saddled it, then returned. Then he said to him, "Do you think you can ride it?" He said, "Yes." So he rode it without it resisting him. Then he galloped it in the residence, then set it to a graceful gait, and it walked in the finest manner possible. Then he returned and dismounted.

Then al-Mustaʿīn said to him, "O Abū Muḥammad, how did you find it?" He said, "O Commander of the Faithful, I have not seen its like in beauty and vigor, and it is only fitting that the like of it should belong to the Commander of the Faithful." He said: Then he said, "O Abū Muḥammad, the Commander of the Faithful has bestowed it upon you." So Abū Muḥammad said to my father, "O boy, take it." So my father took it and led it away.

key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ: the kunyah of Imam al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام in this report
key_terms.السَّرْجَ: the saddle placed on the animal for riding
key_terms.اللِّجَامَ: the bridle placed on the animal
key_terms.الْبَيْطَرَةَ: veterinary practice or treatment of animals
key_terms.الْمُسْتَعِينِ: Al-Mustaʿīn, the Abbasid ruler mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْهَمْلَجَةِ: a graceful, brisk, elegant gait in riding
key_terms.بَغْلٌ: a mule central to the event of the narration

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe a sign of Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام through the taming of al-Mustaʿīn’s mule?
ai.summary: This report narrates an episode in which Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام was summoned before al-Mustaʿīn to deal with an exceptionally difficult mule that no one could control. By the Imam’s presence and action, the animal became subdued, and he then bridled, saddled, and rode it with ease, after which it was gifted to him. The narration highlights a sign of the Imam’s distinction and the political atmosphere surrounding him.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Abu Ali Muhammad Bin Ali Bin Ibrahim who said, ‘Ahmad Bin Al Haris Al Qazwiny narrated to me saying,

‘I was with my father at Surmanrayy (Samarrah), and my father was a vet in the stables of Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>). And it was so that with Al-Mustain (Caliph) was a mule the likes of which has not been seen regarding beauty, and age, and it used to forbid its back (for riding), and the reining, and the saddling. And the trainers had gathered upon it but it did not enable a way to them with regards to riding it.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So one of his close aides said to him, ‘O commander of the faithful! Why don’t you send for Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, the son<sup>asws</sup> of Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> until he<sup>asws</sup> comes over, so either he<sup>asws</sup> would (be able to) ride it or it would kill him<sup>asws</sup>, so you would be at rest from him<sup>asws</sup>’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So he sent for Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>, and my father went with him<sup>asws</sup>. So my father said, ‘When Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> entered the house, I was with him<sup>asws</sup>, and Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> looked at the mule paused in the courtyard of the house, and he<sup>asws</sup> went to it and placed his<sup>asws</sup> hand upon its back. So I looked at the mule and it had perspired, to the extent that its perspiration was flowing from it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> came to Al-Mu’tasim, so he greeted upon him<sup>asws</sup> and welcomed him<sup>asws</sup> and sat him<sup>asws</sup> close by, and he said, ‘O Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>! Harness this mule’. So Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> said to my father, ‘Harness it, O boy!’. So Al-Mu’tasim said, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> harness it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> dropped his<sup>asws</sup> pallium, then he<sup>asws</sup> stood up and harnessed, then returned to his<sup>asws</sup> seat and sat down.

So he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>! Saddle it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to my father: ‘O boy, saddle it!’ So he said, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> saddle it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> stood up for the second time and saddle it, and returned. So he said, ‘Do you<sup>asws</sup> view that you<sup>asws</sup> can ride it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> rode it from without it preventing upon him<sup>asws</sup>. Then he<sup>asws</sup> ran it in the house, then he<sup>asws</sup> spurred it upon encouragement, so it walked with as excellently as could happen to be. Then he<sup>asws</sup> returned and desended.

So Al-Mu’tasim said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>! How did you<sup>asws</sup> see it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘O commander of the faithful! I<sup>asws</sup> have not seen as excellent as it in beauty and agility, and it is not correct that the like of it should be with anyone except for the commander of the faithful’. So he said, ‘O Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>! Supposing the commander of the faithful has burdens you<sup>asws</sup> upon it?’ So Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> said to my father: ‘O boy! Take it’. So my father took it and led it away’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, known as ibn al-Kurdiy, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“We were under pressure and constraint. My father said, “Let us go to abu Muhammad (a.s.). People describe him as very generous and considerate.” I asked, “Do you know him?” He said, “No, I do not know him and I have not seen him before.” We decided to go and meet him. My father said on the way, “I wish he would grant us five hundred Dirhams. Two hundred for clothes, two hundred for to pay the debts and two hundred for expenses. We need this much very badly.” I then said to myself, “I wish he will grant me three hundred Dirhams, one hundred to buy a donkey, one hundred for expenses and one hundred for clothes to go to the mountains.”

The narrator has said that when we arrived at the door a slave came out and said, “Ali ibn Ibrahim and his son Muhammad come inside.” When we were in his (the Imam’s (a.s.) presence we offered the greeting of peace and said to my father. “O Ali, what held you back from coming to us until now?” He said, “My master, I felt shy to come to you in this condition.”

When we left him his slave came to us and gave a bag of money to my father saying, “This is five hundred Dirhams, two hundred for clothes, two hundred to pay debts and two hundred for expenses.” He gave me a bag and said, “This is three hundred Dirhams, one hundred for the donkey, one hundred for clothes and one hundred for expenses. Do not go to the mountains. Go to Sawra’.
He then went to Sawra’ and marriage a woman and now his income from properties is a thousand Dinar despite this he belongs to the waqifi sect in matters of beliefs.

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim has said that I said to him, “Woe is you! What more clear proof do you want to believe in him as your Imam?” He said, “This (belief in Waqifi sect) is habit that has been with us (and it ddoes not go away).”
